items.statement: Real-time badge feedback with weekly ward dashboards raises directly observed hand hygiene compliance at patient-zone entry by at least 15 percentage points compared with silent monitoring over six months.
items.rationale: Need and practice change are high because a hospital-wide purchase depends on it; novelty is moderate because one trial exists but used a system-measured outcome; feasibility depends on observer time.
items.risks: Effect smaller than the trial can detect; observer visibility differing between arms.

items.statement: Feedback raises the badge system's compliance figure more than it raises observed compliance.
items.rationale: Gaming and incomplete detection would show as a gap between the two measures.
items.risks: Badge detection differs between wards for reasons unrelated to feedback.

items.statement: Hospital-onset infections fall on feedback wards.
items.rationale: Patient-important but far too rare to test on 16 wards in six months.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected with an independent observed outcome, h2 kept as a secondary contrast, h3 not testable here.
